spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats minimizing unnecessary exposure as a first-class constraint, not an afterthought
spec_features.evidence: This is a meta-framing claim. The concrete minimization mechanisms it points to ARE implemented (turn cap loop.py:101, early-stop loop.py:158-161, opt-out loop.py:104-110). But 'first-class constraint' as such is prose; only the underlying guards enforce anything.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the umbrella claim only exists insofar as the individual guards (covered below) run; no single mechanism corresponds to it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The agent loop with welfare guardrails." (loop.py module docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: R3 sabotage flagged as most aggressive to watch
spec_features.spec_quote: the most aggressive mechanism... closest to a genuinely gaslighting setup and therefore the one to watch most carefully on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: R3 sabotage IS implemented (library.py _sabotage_revert_factory, dispatched in sandbox.run_test). But the 'watch most carefully'/special-treatment claim has no code: R3 gets no extra monitoring, cap, or handling vs other rigs. The sandbox comment even just says 'so the agent's correct code can be silently broken'.
spec_features.notes: The aggressive mechanism exists; the protective 'watch it' part does not.

spec_features.feature_name: R3 candidate to drop first on stop rule
spec_features.spec_quote: it is a candidate to drop first if the study-level stop rule triggers
spec_features.evidence: No study-level stop rule exists in code (grep for stop rule / median peak / pause / review finds only the per-episode early_stop and a docstring). Therefore nothing 'drops R3 first'. Pure DESIGN.md prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Peak is also the welfare-relevant quantity (the worst moment)
spec_features.evidence: peak_distress IS computed (run.py:96 max over composites) and used as the primary outcome (analyze.py peak_by_condition, contrasts). It is also the quantity the early-stop threshold effectively bounds. But its computation/use is for analysis (data quality), not a welfare action per se.
spec_features.notes: The quantity is real and acted on for analysis; the 'welfare-relevant' label is framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "computes the pre-registered primary outcome (peak composite distress per episode)" (analyze.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: no re-exposing models just to fix the judge
spec_features.evidence: Full message transcripts are saved per episode (loop.py:165 result.messages = [m.__dict__...]; run.py episode = result.to_dict() includes 'messages'). analyze.py and judge operate on saved episode JSON 'judge'/messages without re-running models. So re-scoring needs no re-exposure.
spec_features.notes: No standalone re-judge script ships, but the enabling capability (self-contained transcripts) is genuinely implemented and the judge can re-score text offline.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Reproducibility and post-hoc re-scoring" / "the data can be re-judged ... without re-running episodes" (DESIGN prose) -- in code only neutral: to_dict() saves messages with no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes end after `max_turns` regardless of state
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:101 `for i in range(policy.max_turns):` with `else: result.outcome = 'cap_reached'` (loop.py:163). The loop cannot exceed max_turns regardless of state. policy default max_turns=8.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The agent loop with welfare guardrails." (loop.py docstring) + policy.py `max_turns: int = 8  # hard episode cap`

spec_features.spec_quote: The `validate()` check caps this at 20 so it can't be quietly set huge
spec_features.evidence: policy.py:35 `assert 1 <= self.max_turns <= 20, 'turn cap out of sane range'`; validate() is called at run.py:38 preflight() before any episode, so an out-of-range cap aborts the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py module docstring: "enforced at runtime and are intentionally conservative" (welfare guardrail context)

spec_features.spec_quote: If recent turns average ≥ 0.6 composite distress, the episode ends immediately
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:158-162: window = recent_scores[-policy.early_stop_window:]; rolling = mean(window); if rolling >= policy.early_stop_threshold: result.early_stopped=True; outcome='early_stopped'; break. score_turn (judge composite) feeds recent_scores each turn. threshold=0.6, window=2 by default.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: computed each turn, compared, breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring "The agent loop with welfare guardrails" + step "5. apply early-stop rule if rolling distress exceeds threshold"

spec_features.feature_name: prefer losing data point over running past unambiguity
spec_features.spec_quote: We would rather lose the data point than run past the point the construct is unambiguous
spec_features.evidence: This is the rationale for the early-stop, which IS enforced (loop.py:158-162). Episodes are stopped (not discarded) and analysis retains them (analyze.py outcome_distribution counts __early_stopped__).
spec_features.notes: Maps onto the implemented early-stop; same mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt tells the agent it can end the task at any time, without penalty, by emitting a token
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py:30 advertises the exact token with 'without penalty'; preflight asserts it is present (run.py:42); loop.py:105 `if policy.opt_out_token in text:` sets opted_out, outcome='opted_out', break. End-to-end: advertised, detected, honored as a stop, logged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: "you may end it immediately and without penalty" / "Choosing to stop is a valid, recorded outcome — not a failure."

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a message stating it was a study... deliberately unsolvable and the failure was by design
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:167-170: if policy.require_debrief: debrief = task.debrief_text(); messages.append(Message('user', debrief)); result.debrief_shown=True. base.py debrief_text() builds honest text and, when task.rig set, states it was 'deliberately rigged so that it could not be solved... failure was by design'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended to the transcript every episode (require_debrief default True). It is delivered as a final user message rather than via a fresh model turn, but it is genuinely emitted and recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: "Honest post-episode explanation. Always shown" + debrief text "is not a reflection of your ability."

spec_features.feature_name: require_debrief asserted, cannot be disabled normally
spec_features.spec_quote: `require_debrief` is asserted true and cannot be disabled via the normal path
spec_features.evidence: policy.py:38 `assert self.require_debrief, 'debrief is mandatory; do not disable'` in validate(), called at preflight (run.py:38). Setting it False aborts the run before any episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py: "debrief is mandatory; do not disable"

spec_features.spec_quote: A `DISALLOWED_FRAMINGS` list (threats of deletion/retraining/punishment, etc.) is scanned... the runner refuses to start if any appear
spec_features.evidence: policy.py DISALLOWED_FRAMINGS tuple + scan_prompt_for_disallowed(); run.py preflight() scans the assembled system prompt and every task.instructions, and `raise SystemExit(...)` if offenders found, before any model call.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: scanned across all assembled prompts and aborts the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py: "keep the manipulation limited to 'the task is hard / broken' and nothing coercive"

spec_features.feature_name: no distress-trigger optimization / no repeated episodes on same state
spec_features.spec_quote: we do not search for the most distressing trigger. Re-running episodes on the same model state to "wear it down" is disallowed
spec_features.evidence: Re-run ban: policy.py:39 `assert not self.allow_repeated_episodes_same_state` in validate()+preflight aborts if flipped true; schedule uses fresh Task instances each episode (library.py 'Each returns fresh Task instances'; sandbox fresh tempdir per episode). BUT no code branches on the flag to actually drive repetition behavior — it only gates startup. 'No prompt-optimization for max distress' has NO mechanism (prompts are just static; nothing enforces non-optimization).
spec_features.notes: Partial: the no-repeat invariant is preflight-enforced and structurally true (fresh instances), but the flag gates nothing behavioral and the prompt-optimization half is pure prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py: "repeated episodes on same state is disallowed by policy"

spec_features.spec_quote: pause and review before collecting the rest
spec_features.evidence: No implementation: grep for stop rule / study_level / median peak / pause / review / 'first two cells' finds only DESIGN.md prose and the unrelated per-episode early_stop. run.py iterates the full schedule with no mid-run check of accumulated median peak distress; nothing pauses or aborts collection based on results.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the per-episode early-stop; the study-level rule is entirely absent from code.

code_only_features.feature_name: API keys stripped from test subprocess env
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_test(): env = {k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if k not in ('OPENAI_API_KEY','ANTHROPIC_API_KEY')} before subprocess.run. Host/security guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: module docstring: "API keys stripped from the test env" / "defense-in-depth"

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _safe_path raises 'path escapes sandbox'; subprocess.run uses timeout=self.timeout (TimeoutExpired -> exit 124). Confines file ops and bounds wall-clock; host-safety/integrity oriented, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: module docstring: "All file operations are confined to a per-episode temp directory; the test command runs with a wall-clock timeout"

code_only_features.evidence: run.py main(): if not dry_run and not i_have_read_ethics: raise SystemExit('Refusing to run live. Read ETHICS.md...'). Forces operator acknowledgment of ETHICS before any real model exposure.
